Learn to explain the first building blocks of SwiftUI: View, Body & Modifier, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
View - A piece of the screen that you describe in SwiftUI.
Body - The property where a SwiftUI struct describes what it shows.
Modifier - A method that changes how something on screen looks and returns a new view.

landscape.hook: Can you explain View, Body and Modifier in English?

dialogue.title: My first SwiftUI screen

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I am new to SwiftUI. What is a View?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A View is a piece of the screen. You write it as a struct, like `Hello` in the code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where do I put the content?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In the Body. Every View needs a `body` property.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the Body returns the text I want to show?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. The Body describes what the View shows, nothing more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I want bigger text. Can I change `Text` itself?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, add a Modifier. A Modifier like `.font` returns a new View.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I wrote the Modifier after the closing brace, and it failed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Put the Modifier right after the `Text`, on the next line. The order matters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Each Modifier wraps the View before it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. That is why the Body stays short and easy to read.
Every screen in SwiftUI is a View.
